status: Five native owned commands register with Pi's names and descriptions and run through the host dialogs and UI ports. Manifests and the non-mutating upstream flow traces match the unchanged extension. Loaded-library RPC acceptance belongs to the native integration lane.
compared: pi.registerCommand order, names and descriptions captured from the unchanged extensions/multiprovider.ts under Node 24.22.0
The {version:1,name,description} manifest passed to register_native_command, in registration order
The {version:1,command,args} request envelope and {version:1,result}|{version:1,error} response envelope
context/snapshot as the source of hasUI, so a detached UI shows no control and sends no notification
dialogs/show controls (select, confirm, input, settings) and the validated reply shape; a null or type=cancel reply is a cancellation
ui/notify text and kind ordering, projected unchanged from Pi's ctx.ui.notify
Upstream traces for /multilogin, /multilogout, /accounts, /switch-account and /vprovider replayed through the native entry point, compared as whole JSON values
Cancellation stops a pending dialog and returns the host's cancellation error
Missing owned-command slots, missing native runtime port, refused registration, unknown command, unsupported version, malformed JSON, non-string args and a short cancellation control
notTested: No loaded-library/RPC run: the registration path here calls the same extern "C" callback through a fake PluginApi vtable, not through rpi's extension loader. The native integration lane owns the loaded acceptance.

The 16 replayed scenarios are the non-mutating subset: they read the session view, provider registry and service snapshot. Store writes, logins, pool-manager edits and session pin entries stay covered by tests/commands.rs and tests/commands_a2.rs.

Port::mode (ctx.mode) is supplied by the integration owner's CommandHost; this lane reads hasUI from the host but does not force a mode. A wrong Port::mode can still let a TUI-only command run outside the TUI.
The Arc-backed callback contexts are released when the owning Commands handle is dropped in the plugin's finish_shutdown hook; if that hook is skipped the runtime threads leak until process exit.
